**Kevin Scott**, Microsoft’s CTO, predicts that **95% of all code will be AI-generated by 2030**, a shift he describes as moving developers from "input masters" of programming languages to "prompt masters" who orchestrate AI systems.

While AI will handle the bulk of code generation, Scott emphasizes that **human authorship remains critical** for high-level design, problem-solving, and defining software intent. He compares this transition to the industry's historical shift from Assembly to high-level languages, noting that AI will enable **smaller, more agile teams** to build complex, enterprise-scale software that previously required large groups of engineers.
